display.title: Episode 390: The Island of Treasures (Tu B'Av)
display.summary_short: On Tu B'Av, Uncle Yossi urges adding Torah study; a shipwrecked man made king of an island spends its treasures there, a parable for using this world to prepare for the next.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the night of Chamisha Asar B'Av 5749. Uncle Yossi explains, from the Mishnah, that Israel had no days as joyous as the fifteenth of Av, and that the custom from this day on is to add more time to Torah learning, by day and especially at night, and to encourage friends to do the same. After the Hakochainik march and the sponsor, a ten-year-old girl recites the Shema and tells of receiving a dollar and a blessing from the Rebbe. Introducing Pirkei Avos chapter 4, read that Shabbos, he teaches that this world is a hallway before the banquet hall of the World to Come. The story: Yisrael, sole survivor of a shipwreck, is crowned king of an island and spends its whole treasury beautifying it, only to learn that each king must leave in rags when the next castaway arrives; too late, he wishes he had sent treasures home. The island is this world, the treasures are mitzvos, and the Torah is the key. The show closes with an invitation to send in essays and poems, a call to sign up friends for Tzivos Hashem during the summer, and the Shabbos candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: This world is a hallway to the next; send ahead treasures of Torah and mitzvos while you can.

advisories.note: A ship sinks in a storm and only one passenger survives.
